newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury sees $48 bln Q4 borrowing need.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury sees $48 bln Q4 borrowing need.

text.p: The Treasury Department announced on Monday that its estimated net market borrowing need in the October-December fourth quarter will be $48 billion, assuming a cash balance of $30 billion on Dec 30.
During the July-September third quarter, Treasury said its actual net borrowing was $40.3 billion and that it had an end-of-quarter cash balance of $44.2 billion.
Looking ahead to the first quarter of 1997, Treasury estimated it would need to borrow a net $50 billion to $55 billion in the three months from January through March.
Treasury has scheduled a news conference on Wednesday at 1300EDT/1700GMT to announce details of its plans for selling three- and 10-year notes and 30-year bonds next week to meet its borrowing needs.

Originally, Treasury had estimated it would need to borrow $45 billion during the third quarter this year and that its end-of-quarter cash balance would be only $40 billion. But its actual borrowing was lower.
"The combined $8.9 billion improvement was the result of higher than estimated receipts and lower than estimated outlays," Treasury said.
